candidates.title: Directedly balance codeword geometry while preserving transition separation
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the cold run's exported level-0 Gini exceeds the control's 0.216, L1-to-L2 branches fall below 65.91 per L1 code, train-to-test frequency drift grows, sequence information falls, or the single held-out Stage-3 recall@10 does not exceed 0.06406796775709883.
candidates.risk: Uniform soft usage and a centroid-spread barrier may preserve code usage without preserving useful item distinctions; the directed KL can also over-separate common transitions. The soft objective may not translate into hard assignment changes, and the frozen run could therefore fail to improve Stage-3 retrieval despite healthy soft statistics.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The usage-balancing component adjusts codewords through their soft-assignment probabilities, while the centroid barrier repels codewords from an overly tight centroid geometry. The directed KL component penalizes source and target assignment distributions that become indistinguishable. These terms do not minimize the distance between a transition's two codewords; the KL term instead favors different endpoint distributions. A zero barrier gradient can occur when the separation threshold is already met.

candidates.title: Increase directed assignment information with an explicit anti-convergence term
candidates.falsifier: Reject if exported level-0 Gini exceeds 0.216, L1-to-L2 branches fall below 65.91 per L1 code, train-to-test frequency drift grows, sequence information falls, or the single held-out Stage-3 recall@10 does not exceed 0.06406796775709883.
candidates.risk: Assignment separation can encode transition-specific distinctions that are too fine-grained or unstable for held-out transitions. The entropy term balances only the source marginal, so target usage, prefix branching, or train-to-test frequency drift may still worsen; soft separation may also fail to change hard assignments.
candidates.codebook_interaction: Minimizing negative Jensen-Shannon divergence rewards distinguishable source and target assignment distributions; minimizing the overlap penalty directly discourages both endpoints from using the same codes. The source-marginal entropy term discourages concentrated source usage. All three components update codewords through the soft assignments; none minimizes the distance between the two endpoint codewords.

candidates.title: Transport behavior-conditioned residuals through separated codeword roles
candidates.falsifier: Reject if exported level-0 Gini exceeds 0.216, L1-to-L2 branches fall below 65.91 per L1 code, train-to-test frequency drift grows, sequence information falls, or the single held-out Stage-3 recall@10 does not exceed 0.06406796775709883.
candidates.risk: Residual alignment may favor codeword transport directions that fit frequent training transitions but generalize poorly, while overlap and marginal balance may conflict with naturally common transitions. Cosine alignment can also be unstable when the transport vector is near zero; epsilon keeps the calculation finite but does not guarantee useful gradients or improved hard assignments.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The transport-alignment term updates the source- and target-weighted codebook vectors to represent the directed residual. The overlap penalty discourages shared endpoint assignments, and the source-marginal concentration penalty discourages excessive usage imbalance. The alignment term does not minimize the distance between the two endpoint codewords; the overlap penalty actively discourages assignment convergence.
